problems.target_treatment: Assignment of ground-based silver-iodide cloud seeding to Sierra Madre or Medicine Bow during a four-hour experimental unit (EU).

evidence.location: Section 2, Figure 1 explanation, and Table 1 with its caption, pp. 2640-2643
evidence.text: Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot. The authors report 154 EUs, 27 precipitation-QC exclusions, and nine additional generator-performance exclusions, leaving 118 for the primary analysis. The monthly generator-exclusion cells in Table 1 sum to eight, while its margins and the prose report nine; the retained count here follows the authors' reported totals.

evidence.text: The presentation shows the paired design, four-hour measurements, and a 118-case Medicine Bow assignment plot. Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding in winters 2009/10, 2011/12, and 2013/14. These are different diagnostics within the same trial reported in 2018.
